information.faq_usdt_title: What is USDT and how do I use it?
information.faq_usdt_body: USDT (Tether) is a stablecoin — a digital dollar. Each USDT is worth exactly $1. It runs on the Binance Smart Chain (BSC) network, which means transactions are fast and cheap (often under $0.10).
information.faq_usdt_bullet_1: Send USDT — Enter a BSC address and the amount in dollars. The app routes it on-chain.
information.faq_usdt_bullet_2: Receive USDT — Select the USDT tab, share your BSC address or generate an invoice. The payer sends USDT from any supported chain.
information.faq_usdt_bullet_3: Swap with rBTC — You can convert between rBTC (Rootstock Bitcoin) and USDT using built-in swap routes (LI.FI or Symbiosis). This lets you pay for services in whichever currency the other person prefers.
information.faq_ownwallet_title: Can I use my own wallet (MetaMask, Ledger)?
information.faq_ownwallet_body: Yes. You can connect your own wallet — MetaMask, WalletConnect, Trezor, or Ledger — from the Connected tab. This lets you:
information.faq_ownwallet_bullet_1: Send payments directly from your connected wallet instead of the built-in BitTasker wallet. When sending, pick your connected wallet as the source.
information.faq_ownwallet_bullet_2: Receive payments to your connected wallet's address. When creating a receive request, select your connected wallet as the destination.
information.faq_ownwallet_bullet_3: See all your balances in one place — the total balance card at the top of the Connected tab shows the combined value across all your wallets.
information.faq_ownwallet_footer: Your wallet stays connected between visits. The app never has access to your private keys — you confirm every transaction in your wallet.

loan_help.title: How Bitcoin Loans Work
loan_help.intro: Use your Bitcoin to get cash without selling it. Your Bitcoin stays locked as a safety net, and you get dollars to spend. When you're done, return the dollars and get your Bitcoin back.
loan_help.step1_desc: Choose how much Bitcoin you want to use as collateral. It gets locked in a smart contract — no one can touch it but you.
loan_help.step2_desc: Get USD sent straight to your wallet. You can borrow up to 73% of your collateral value.
loan_help.step3_desc: There's no deadline. Pay back some, all, or none — it's up to you. A small interest fee accrues over time.
loan_help.step4_desc: When you repay your loan, your Bitcoin is returned to your wallet immediately. You keep any gains.
loan_help.note: If the value of your Bitcoin drops too low relative to your loan, it may be sold to repay the debt. Keep an eye on your LTV to stay safe.

lending_help.title: How Lending Works
lending_help.intro: Put your dollars to work. You lend your USD through a trusted protocol and earn interest — like a savings account, but often with better rates.
lending_help.step1_desc: Choose how much USDT0 you want to lend. It goes into a secure lending pool managed by smart contracts.
lending_help.step2_desc: Your money earns interest roughly every 12 seconds. It compounds automatically — no action needed on your part.
lending_help.step3_desc: There's no lock-up period. Withdraw some or all of your funds whenever you want, with no penalties.
lending_help.step4_desc: Your earnings update in real time. The longer your dollars stay lent, the more you earn thanks to compounding.
lending_help.note: Your funds are in a battle-tested protocol with billions in assets. Interest rates fluctuate based on supply and demand, so the exact rate may change over time.

lp_help.title: How Earn Fees Works
lp_help.intro: You provide Bitcoin and USD to a trading pool. Every time someone swaps between the two, you earn a share of the trading fee. It's like being a market maker — you supply the liquidity that others trade against.
lp_help.step1_desc: You put in an equal value of Bitcoin (wBTC) and Dollars (USDT0). The pool needs both sides so traders can swap between them.
lp_help.step2_desc: Every trade that uses your liquidity pays a small fee (0.05%). Those fees accumulate in your position and can be collected anytime.
lp_help.step3_desc: If the price of Bitcoin changes a lot while your funds are in the pool, you may end up with more of one asset and less of the other. This is called impermanent loss — it's the main risk of providing liquidity.
lp_help.step4_desc: You can collect your earned fees without removing liquidity. When you're done, close your position to get everything back.
lp_help.note: Your funds are in a Uniswap V3 pool — one of the most widely used DeFi protocols. Returns depend on trading volume and can vary significantly.

gasless_enable.title: Enable Gasless Transactions
